description: A job's status, and its result when it is done. The service keeps every job across its restarts for its retention (a day on the public service); a job that was running when it stopped is run again once from its request (its interruptions say when), and stopped again it comes back interrupted, with the reason.
name: get_quantum_job

anyOf.description: A job as a host returns it: its status, the method its plan chose and why, the request as submitted, and, once it is done, the result with its receipt: a job's result, or for a set (a request with programs or a sweep, its method set) the set's result. The command line's run --json, the local MCP server's run_quantum_circuit and a run on the person's own provider give a finished job; the job service also gives its id and times, and a job still queued or running, or failed with its error. A job's receipt verifies from this document alone: request and result.

digests.description: The job service: the BLAKE3 digests its store keeps the job's objects under (the request, each program, the result and the receipt).

error.description: Why a job failed, or why it was interrupted.

estimate.description: What the plan admitted the job with.

id.description: The job service's id for the job.

interruptions.description: The job service: each time it stopped while the job ran, in milliseconds since 1970. A job that was running when the service stopped is queued again, once, to run from its stored request.

method.description: The method the plan chose; set for a set.

peak_rss_bytes.description: The job service: the most memory the job's process held.

request.description: A job as a client submits it: a program and what is asked of it, or a set: many programs (programs), or one over a grid of its inputs (sweep), run as one job. The command line, both MCP servers, the job service, the desktop app and the Studio read it alike, and a receipt seals it as it was given. A member the engine does not read is ignored, and sealed with the rest.

amplitudes.description: Basis states whose amplitudes to return: one 0 or 1 per qubit, qubit n-1 first.

compile.description: What a compile is asked for, each optional: the most the output may differ from the program (epsilon, in the operator norm up to a global phase), the level (0 lowers and approximates; 1 also rewrites and folds phases; 2 also resynthesises), the basis, the gate set it writes the program in (clifford_t: every rotation off the multiples of π/4 a Clifford+T word; standard: nothing approximated), whether to give the circuit after each pass (stages), and the twirl and dd passes, last (twirl, with its seed; dd, with its sequence).

dd.description: Dynamical decoupling in each window where a qubit idles long enough: xx or xy4 (or {"sequence": …}), checked to change nothing without noise.

twirl.description: Twirl each two-qubit Clifford gate with Paulis drawn from a seeded stream: true (seed 1), or {"seed": N}. One seed is one instance, checked to be the same circuit.

contract.description: What the job wants of an answer (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.7). Every route the host can see is priced with what is really known, those that cannot meet this are rejected, the cheapest of the rest runs, and the reasoning is sealed in the result as `planner`. Nothing falls back in silence, and a job no route can meet is refused (J071). A job without it plans as it always has, byte for byte. Refused on a set (J073).

deadline_seconds.description: When it must be done by, in seconds from when it starts. A route whose time is not known does not meet it. A host that can stop a run stops it there (J074); otherwise the result says whether it was kept.

exactness.description: The class wanted. Without it, the job keeps the class auto would give: auto's pick stands while it meets the rest of the contract, and only a route at least as exact may take its place. A device's counts are in no classical class: measured wants a processor's, simulated a provider's simulator's that its provider does not state is approximate, and any takes every route.

max_cost.description: The most a provider's estimate of the run may come to, before it runs: it bounds the estimate, not the charge, which is stated after the run beside it (kept.cost). A route with an unknown cost, an estimate that is only the least it can come to, or a price in another currency does not meet it: nothing is converted.

amount.description: An amount in decimals: digits, and optionally a point and digits, at most 64 characters.

max_joules.description: The most energy it may take, held by a live reading while it runs: at the ceiling the run is stopped, gives no answer, and its receipt says so. A route nothing here can read and stop does not meet it, so on a host that reads none every route is rejected. An estimate can refuse a job clearly past it, and promises nothing.

providers.description: Whether a route may be one of the person's providers. never is the default, given or not: a job that names a provider under a contract that does not allow one is refused (J070), and a host asks no provider anything under it. A host that reaches none (the job service) lists none. A provider that costs money is chosen only under max_cost, or when the job names it, and still runs only on the person's word for that route and its estimate.

dry_run.description: With true: what the host would do with the job or set, running nothing.

fabric.description: Where the statevector method's state runs: auto (the default: on a member only where the committed measurements show it faster than this host's CPU for the job's size and fusion width, otherwise on the CPU), cpu, accelerator (the first accelerator member certified bit-exact here that holds the state, falling back to the next if it fails during the run), a member's id or key (wai-quantum fabric lists them), or a list of members, a power of two of them, the state split by its top qubits into one partition on each (cpu is a member, and a member may be named more than once). A member certified bit-exact gives the CPU's bits. A placement this host cannot honour is refused (J013), never made elsewhere.

history.description: The program's history's account of the version the job runs: its digest, and the gates and lines in each hand. The receipt binds it; a history recomputes and checks it.

anyOf.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled, with its options.

items.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled, with its options.

intent.description: What the program must do, checked with the run: one intent or a list. The result's verdict says how far it was checked.

method.description: auto (the default: the strongest method the program admits), or a method by its name as the methods list names it; pulse runs a pulse program (OpenPulse calibrations) under the pulse options.

mitigate.description: Mitigate the job's expectation values (or, for readout, its counts) under its noise (engine::mitigate): zne, pea, pec, cdr, vd or readout, or {"method", …} with its options. The result's mitigation gives each value raw and mitigated.

noise.description: A noise model, each channel a probability. A channel not listed here is refused.

observables.description: Pauli observables to take the expectation values of.

anyOf.description: A Pauli string, as "Z0 Z1"; qubits count from 0.

options.description: Options of the method that runs the job, as the methods list names them (max_bond, cutoff, fusion, trajectories, threshold, max_weight, ladder, max_terms, path_restarts, controls), and memory_gb.

controls.description: A gate whose standard gates would double (x, y, z or h under three or more controls; s, sdg, t, tdg, p, rx, ry, rz, u, sx or sxdg under two or more) runs as one on statevector and in standard gates on exact. "standard" runs standard gates on statevector too, which reproduces a result made that way bit for bit. "whole" holds the gate whole on exact too, which gives other bits than its default, and is refused (J003) on a job that runs standard gates: another method named, a compile, noise, mitigation, a device target or a named place on the fabric. Any other value is refused.

params.description: A value for each of the program's parameters (`input float theta;`, `input angle phi;`), bound exactly before the program is read: it runs as if each were written as a `const` at that double. A parameter left without a value is refused (Q114, J050). In a sweep, the parameters it fixes, each bound at every point.

programs.description: A set (engine::sets): the programs to run as one job, each a program's text or a job of its own; the request's other fields apply to every item that does not set them itself.

anyOf.description: A program's text.
A job of its own, read as a job request is (no programs or sweep in it); each item of the set's result holds its request in full.

provider.description: The person's own provider to run on, by the name their registry gives it. Only a host that holds their credentials runs such a job; every other host refuses it.

pulse.description: A pulse run's options (method "pulse"): the sample period, the levels kept, the tolerance on the stated error, the steps a sample is divided into, each qubit's parameters, static couplings, and ports beyond the names d0, m0, a0.

levels.description: Levels kept per qubit (default 2; 3 shows leakage).

ports.description: Ports by name: what each is for and the qubit it reaches.

rabi_mhz.description: Its Rabi frequency at full amplitude, MHz.

qubits.description: Each qubit's parameters by its index, over the target's and the defaults.

substeps.description: Steps per sample (default: chosen so each step times the generator's norm is at most 0.5).

tolerance.description: The most the stated error may be (default 1e-6): a run whose bound and rounding estimate pass it is refused, naming the steps that would meet it.

qasm.description: The program, in OpenQASM 3 or the OpenQASM 2 forms in common use.

repair.description: Repair the program first on its flagged lines: true, or the choices.

seed.description: The sampling seed (1 when not given): the same job and seed give the same counts.

shots.description: Measurement shots; 1024 when no observables or amplitudes are asked for, otherwise 0.

source.description: The program in another format, in place of qasm (engine::formats::expand): read to the job's qasm before the job is read, the request keeping its source.

sweep.description: A set over the request's own qasm: values for each of the program's inputs (integer, float or angle), every combination run, the names in sorted order and the first varying slowest.

anyOf.description: A device target: its qubits, the pairs it couples, its native gates with their errors and durations, and the calibration snapshot they come from. A value not known is left out, never written as zero. Every field but format, name, source, qubits, gates and coupling is optional, and a field the format does not name is refused, so a misspelt one never reads as absent. Its canonical text is its RFC 8785 form, and the BLAKE3 of that text, the target's hash, names the snapshot in a receipt.

id.description: The calibration snapshot's id, as the source names it, or a content id of the snapshot read.

timestamp.description: When the snapshot was taken, as the source writes it.

coupling.description: The pairs a two-qubit gate may act on, each once, the lower qubit first, sorted.

gates.description: Each native gate where the device runs it, sorted by gate then qubits.

label.description: The source's own name for it, when that is not its index.

qubit.description: Its index: its place in the list.

t2_us.description: T2 (the echo or Ramsey time the source reports), microseconds.

format.description: The format the target was read from (wai-quantum targets import --help lists them).

target.description: A device target: a built-in target's name, or a target document. The program is compiled to it, placed and simulated under its noise; noise may not be given beside it.

verdict.description: true: the result carries a verdict even with no intent.

anyOf.description: A job's result as the engine gives it, on every host: what was asked of the program, computed by the method its plan chose, with that method's accuracy class. The receipt seals the result without its receipt member, beside the request. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema); results made before results carried them have neither and follow this schema all the same.

accuracy.description: What the method promises of the numbers it gave.

approximate.description: A simulated result whose provider states its simulator is approximate.

below_table.description: The bit-exact method: phase gates of its lowering that are not zero and ran as no phase, within the reader's tolerance (1e-14 of a turn) of a whole turn. `angles` counts those gates: one angle written may be several, and another count in another form of the same program.

bound.description: The bound this result is held to, by method: a pulse run (class bounded): every probability within this of the exact solution of the model's master equation, the truncation bound and the rounding estimate together; stabilizer_rank's sampled mode (class estimate): the bound on the distance of the estimated state from the state, holding with the probability confidence states.

class.description: bit-exact: the same bits on every machine; exact: no approximation beyond double-precision rounding; single: single-precision arithmetic; bounded: a rigorous bound beside each value; estimate: a statistical estimate with its standard error; heuristic: an approximation with an estimate of its error, not a bound; measured: counts a processor returned through the person's provider, not reproducible by recomputation; simulated: counts a provider's simulator or emulator returned, measured on no device. Results sealed before simulated existed label a provider's simulator measured, and are read by its provenance. none: the run was stopped at its contract's energy ceiling and gave no answer.

confidence.description: The probability a stated bound holds.

global_phase.description: The bit-exact method: method statevector's state of the program that ran is e^(i radians) times the amplitudes given, since this method's lowering drops the phase of rz, rx, ry, rxx, ryy, rzz and u. Absent when that is 1. The language's own state can differ from both: its U is e^(i theta / 2) times the matrix both methods take as u, the reader drops an uncontrolled gphase (Q206), and a compiled job's program is the compile's, right up to a global phase.

radians.description: The same in radians, in (-pi, pi].

turns_over_2_33.description: The phase exactly, in 2^33rds of a turn.

moved_angles.description: The bit-exact method: phase gates of its lowering within the reader's tolerance (1e-14 of a turn) of a dyadic angle, by more than a double's rounding of it, that ran as it. `angles` counts those gates.

rounding_estimate.description: A pulse run: an estimate of floating-point rounding beside the bound, not a proof.

t_count.description: stabilizer_rank: the T and T† gates the program lowers to.

terms.description: stabilizer_rank: the stabilizer branches summed (2^t exactly), or drawn.

truncation_bound.description: A pulse run: the proved bound, in the trace norm, on what the integrator's series leaves out.

bits.description: One 0 or 1 per qubit, qubit n-1 first.

bound.description: A bound on |exact − value| of the amplitude, holding with the probability confidence states (stabilizer_rank's sampled mode).

calibration.description: A provider job: the calibration snapshot it ran under.

anyOf.description: A provider job: the program sent, compiled exactly to the device's own gates: its basis (the device's gate set), its OpenQASM 3 text (qasm3) and that text's BLAKE3 (program), its counts of gates and swaps, its layouts, and the check it passed before it was sent. Results sealed before qasm3 carry the hash alone.

placement.description: Where the program was placed on the device's qubits, and why.

qasm3.description: The program sent, as OpenQASM 3, $i being index i of the coupling map the provider described; program is the BLAKE3 of its UTF-8 bytes.

qubit_names.description: The device's own name for each index the program uses, as it was when the job was sent, where a client sends it under those names.

anyOf.description: A job asked to compile its program first: what ran is the compiled circuit, within distance of the program in the operator norm up to a global phase.

basis.description: The gate set the program was compiled to.

certificate.description: The BLAKE3 of the compile certificate's RFC 8785 text, in hex.

distance.description: The bound the passes' distances add to.

output.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

source.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

compiled.description: How the program was compiled before it ran: on the person's own provider, to the device's gates; or, asked with compile, to a basis within a budget. Either way, basis is the gate set it was compiled to.

components.description: The identity of every component that made the result, when a registered one took part (engine::registry): its program's format, the passes its compile ran, the noise channels it names, its method; each registered one marked so. Sealed by the receipt with the rest.

items.description: One component that made the result (engine::registry): its kind, name and version, the BLAKE3 digest of its descriptor, and whether it is built in. A result carries these only when a registered component took part; one made by built-ins alone names them as it always has (its method, its compile's passes, its noise's channels and the engine's version), the digests of that version listed by the components list.

certified.description: Beside a registered component: the engine does not certify it.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the component's descriptor in its canonical JSON (engine::registry::digest_of).

origin.description: built-in: the engine's own; registered: a host's own, added in its process, not part of the engine.

cost.description: A provider job: the estimate shown before it was sent, what the provider says it charged, and whether the person confirmed a run that was not free.

counts.description: Outcomes and their counts, keyed by the program's classical bits, the highest bit first. At most 65536 outcomes are listed; omitted_shots holds the rest.

counts_source.description: A provider job: where its counts come from (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.3): tallied from one record a shot (shots), the provider's own counts (vendor_counts), or rebuilt from the probabilities it returned by largest remainders, derived and not shot records (probabilities). Results sealed before it carry neither it nor execution.

diagnostics.description: The reader's warnings and notes on the program, each with its code.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

dynamic.description: A program that measures in the middle, resets or branches on a measured bit: how it ran.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall time of the run, where the host has a clock (not in a browser tab).

service_kwh.description: A provider job: the provider's own figure.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

execution.description: A provider job: how the device was asked to run the program (section 8.3): who states it (stated_by: client, provider or nobody); what the client sent (sent: the request's members and the settings among them); each of mitigation, twirling, decoupling, remapping and optimisation (off, on, default when the request sets nothing for it, none when the device has no such step, unknown when nobody states it); whether the gates were to run as written (verbatim); and a note.

decoupling.description: What happened to one step: off or on (by a setting the client sent, or as the provider states), default (the request sets nothing for it, so the provider's default stands), none (the device has no such step), unknown (nobody states it).

mitigation.description: What happened to one step: off or on (by a setting the client sent, or as the provider states), default (the request sets nothing for it, so the provider's default stands), none (the device has no such step), unknown (nobody states it).

optimisation.description: What happened to one step: off or on (by a setting the client sent, or as the provider states), default (the request sets nothing for it, so the provider's default stands), none (the device has no such step), unknown (nobody states it).

remapping.description: What happened to one step: off or on (by a setting the client sent, or as the provider states), default (the request sets nothing for it, so the provider's default stands), none (the device has no such step), unknown (nobody states it).

twirling.description: What happened to one step: off or on (by a setting the client sent, or as the provider states), default (the request sets nothing for it, so the provider's default stands), none (the device has no such step), unknown (nobody states it).

bound.description: A bound on |exact − value|: rigorous for the bounded class; with confidence beside it, holding with that probability.

confidence.description: The probability the bound holds, for a bound that holds with a stated probability (stabilizer_rank's sampled mode).

ladder.description: The value at thresholds a decade apart, the asked one last.

stderr.description: The standard error, for an estimate.

value.description: The coefficient times the expectation value.

fabric.description: Where the state vector, or the pauli method's sum of terms, ran: the kernel, the placement the job asked for, the member that ran it (or each partition's), each with its certificate, and the energy. Present when the job asked for a placement, or when auto placed the state on a member by measurement (`auto`); a job auto leaves on the CPU names nothing; the receipt seals it with the rest of the result. Every member placed is certified bit-exact, so the answers are the CPU's, byte for byte.

asked.description: The placement the job asked for, as it gave it.

auto.description: Why auto placed the state where it ran: the rule (a member is placed only where the committed measurements show it faster than this host's CPU for the job's size and fusion width) and the measured row it rests on, with the host, the day and the load it was measured under. Present only when auto placed a state on a member.

basis.description: The measured row the job is judged by: the largest measured size at or below its own, the launches of its plan, the runs of each, and the spread of the CPU's and the member's times in milliseconds.

cpu_ms.description: The least, the median and the most of a measured row's runs, in milliseconds.

member_ms.description: The least, the median and the most of a measured row's runs, in milliseconds.

discovery_ms.description: What discovering and certifying the host's members took, once per process, as measured.

measured.description: The day the host was measured (UTC).

exchanges.description: Partition qubits exchanged with local ones through the host's copy of the state.

fell_back_from.description: An accelerator request whose member failed during the run: each member that failed, in turn, with how; the member named above ran the job.

gates.description: The program's gates, in standard gates (at most 2^53 - 1), however the method ran them.

global_phase.description: Why the amplitudes' global phase is not fixed, when it is not.

ideal.description: A provider job: the circuit's exact distribution set beside the measured counts.

job.description: A provider job: the provider's job id and its status checks.

method.description: The method that ran the job (provider for a run on the person's own provider).

mitigation.description: A job's mitigation (its request's mitigate, engine::mitigate), in its result: the method and the options it ran with, its bias and variance assumptions, each observable raw and mitigated with a standard error each and the ideal value (or, for readout, the counts inverted as a quasi-distribution), the method's own details and what it spent. docs/qec.md describes each method.

cost.description: The circuits and shots it spent beyond the job's own.

details.description: The method's own: the folded scales and the folding check (zne), the learned model and the amplified values (pea), the quasi-probability and the value it converges to (pec), the training fits (cdr), the purity (vd), the flip and its amplification (readout).

distribution.description: readout: each outcome's raw share and its mitigated quasi-probability, with its standard error.

operations.description: When the method held a gate under many controls as one (statevector, and exact asked for it): the operations it ran.

outcome_dimension.description: The stabilizer method: the dimension of the measured outcomes' affine space.

outputs.description: The program's output declarations: each its name and type, and its value, or the places of its bits in each outcome.

value.description: A number, a boolean, a bit string, a duration's text, {"re", "im"}, or an array of them.

planner.description: Why this route ran (wai.quantum.planner/1): every route the host could see, each one's price or reason for rejection, and the choice. Sealed by the receipt; a verifier recomputes each route's outcome and the choice from what it states (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.7). A plan carries it too, with the refusal in place of the choice when no route meets the contract.

auto.description: The route auto picks, when the job leaves the method to it.

kept.description: What the contract asked, against what happened; each kept is null when it cannot be said. A result that missed one is sealed and says so.

named.description: The route the job names: the provider or the method its request names, or the one method a device target's job runs on; null when it names none.

question.description: The question the job asks, read from its request, which orders the methods auto tries (section 8.7).

refusal.description: When no route meets the contract, in a plan: the refusal as data.

items.description: One route the planner could see: its class, its price or why it has none, and what came of it.

auto_rank.description: On a local route: its rank in auto's order for the job's question, or null where auto does not try it; a built-in method's is section 8.7's table.

class.description: The accuracy class its result has at worst: a matrix product state's is heuristic, though its result may say exact.

host_dependent.description: Whether it depends on the host: a provider's, a method on a GPU, or a registered method.

anyOf.description: What a route costs, with what is really known: a method's memory and work as the planner counts them and its time at the planner's nominal rate; a provider's own estimate, with what that leaves out.

joules.description: An estimate of what the run takes, from past runs, never a promise. A contract's max_joules is enforced by a live reading while the run goes; an estimate can only refuse a job clearly past a ceiling.

leakage.description: With three levels: each qubit's final probability of level 2.

outcome_bits.description: What each character of an outcome is, left to right: a program bit (c[0]) or a qubit ($0).

populations.description: The final state read on every simulated qubit, the highest qubit first, a level above 0 read as 1.

read.description: What the distribution reads: the captures together (into the program's bits when each writes one), or the final state.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

repaired.description: A job asked to repair its program first: the program that ran, each repair, and what needs a person.

shadow.description: A classical method's answer beside a provider's, and their distance, for a contract job a provider answered; or why there is none. Its request can be run again by anyone, to the same counts.

accuracy.description: What the method promises of the numbers it gave.

approximate.description: A simulated result whose provider states its simulator is approximate.

below_table.description: The bit-exact method: phase gates of its lowering that are not zero and ran as no phase, within the reader's tolerance (1e-14 of a turn) of a whole turn. `angles` counts those gates: one angle written may be several, and another count in another form of the same program.

class.description: bit-exact: the same bits on every machine; exact: no approximation beyond double-precision rounding; single: single-precision arithmetic; bounded: a rigorous bound beside each value; estimate: a statistical estimate with its standard error; heuristic: an approximation with an estimate of its error, not a bound; measured: counts a processor returned through the person's provider, not reproducible by recomputation; simulated: counts a provider's simulator or emulator returned, measured on no device. confidence.description: The probability a stated bound holds.

global_phase.description: The bit-exact method: method statevector's state of the program that ran is e^(i radians) times the amplitudes given, since this method's lowering drops the phase of rz, rx, ry, rxx, ryy, rzz and u. turns_over_2_33.description: The phase exactly, in 2^33rds of a turn.

rounding_estimate.description: A pulse run: an estimate of floating-point rounding beside the bound, not a proof.

t_count.description: stabilizer_rank: the T and T† gates the program lowers to.

terms.description: stabilizer_rank: the stabilizer branches summed (2^t exactly), or drawn.

truncation_bound.description: A pulse run: the proved bound, in the trace norm, on what the integrator's series leaves out.

sampling_tvd_bound.description: A bound on the total variation the shots alone leave between two samples of one distribution, on average (section 8.7): each outcome's pooled count split as a fair coin splits it.

shots.description: The shots, where the method names them in the result (trajectories, provider).

state_hash.description: The bit-exact method's statevector hash (BLAKE3, hex): the same on every machine.

stopped.description: A run stopped at its contract's max_joules by a live reading: it gave no answer, and accuracy.class is none (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.7).

read.description: What read the run, and what that covers.

timing.description: A program that states durations (delay, box, stretch) the method does not apply: said so, with the reader's code.

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer about a program, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided). A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was and how it was made.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

impossible.description: The outcomes sampled that the stated distribution gives probability 0: the first 64, in order.

impossible_outcomes.description: How many outcomes sampled the stated distribution gives probability 0.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

parsed.description: Whether the reader took the program, and its warnings and notes with their codes, or its refusal.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

text.description: The refusal as the reader wrote it, with its line and code.

rank.description: The level's place on the ladder, from 0 (refused) to 4 (proof).

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

repairs.description: Each edit a repair made, with the code it answered and the lines it changed.

statement.description: The level in one plain line.

anyOf.description: A set's result: many programs, or one program over a grid of its inputs, run as one job (engine::sets). Its head holds the count, how many items finished and failed, the Merkle root over the items' leaves, the set's energy and time; the set's receipt seals the set's request and its head. Each item is a plain job with its own receipt, its index, its point in a sweep, and its path to the root, so it is shown sealed by the set alone. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema).

service_kwh.description: A provider job: the provider's own figure.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

items.description: One item: its index, its point in a sweep, its request (a plain job, complete in itself), and its result with its own receipt, or why it failed; and its path to the set's root.

path.description: The item's leaf's sibling digests up to the root, in hex.

point.description: A sweep's item: the value of each input it was run at.

request.description: A job as a client submits it: a program and what is asked of it, or a set: many programs (programs), or one over a grid of its inputs (sweep), run as one job. The command line, both MCP servers, the job service, the desktop app and the Studio read it alike, and a receipt seals it as it was given. A member the engine does not read is ignored, and sealed with the rest.

amplitudes.description: Basis states whose amplitudes to return: one 0 or 1 per qubit, qubit n-1 first.

compile.description: What a compile is asked for, each optional: the most the output may differ from the program (epsilon, in the operator norm up to a global phase), the level (0 lowers and approximates; 1 also rewrites and folds phases; 2 also resynthesises), the basis, the gate set it writes the program in (clifford_t: every rotation off the multiples of π/4 a Clifford+T word; standard: nothing approximated), whether to give the circuit after each pass (stages), and the twirl and dd passes, last (twirl, with its seed; dd, with its sequence).

dd.description: Dynamical decoupling in each window where a qubit idles long enough: xx or xy4 (or {"sequence": …}), checked to change nothing without noise.

twirl.description: Twirl each two-qubit Clifford gate with Paulis drawn from a seeded stream: true (seed 1), or {"seed": N}. One seed is one instance, checked to be the same circuit.

contract.description: What the job wants of an answer (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.7). Every route the host can see is priced with what is really known, those that cannot meet this are rejected, the cheapest of the rest runs, and the reasoning is sealed in the result as `planner`. Nothing falls back in silence, and a job no route can meet is refused (J071). A job without it plans as it always has, byte for byte. Refused on a set (J073).

deadline_seconds.description: When it must be done by, in seconds from when it starts. A route whose time is not known does not meet it. A host that can stop a run stops it there (J074); otherwise the result says whether it was kept.

exactness.description: The class wanted. Without it, the job keeps the class auto would give: auto's pick stands while it meets the rest of the contract, and only a route at least as exact may take its place. A device's counts are in no classical class: measured wants a processor's, simulated a provider's simulator's that its provider does not state is approximate, and any takes every route.

max_cost.description: The most a provider's estimate of the run may come to, before it runs: it bounds the estimate, not the charge, which is stated after the run beside it (kept.cost). A route with an unknown cost, an estimate that is only the least it can come to, or a price in another currency does not meet it: nothing is converted.

amount.description: An amount in decimals: digits, and optionally a point and digits, at most 64 characters.

max_joules.description: The most energy it may take, held by a live reading while it runs: at the ceiling the run is stopped, gives no answer, and its receipt says so. A route nothing here can read and stop does not meet it, so on a host that reads none every route is rejected. An estimate can refuse a job clearly past it, and promises nothing.

providers.description: Whether a route may be one of the person's providers. never is the default, given or not: a job that names a provider under a contract that does not allow one is refused (J070), and a host asks no provider anything under it. A host that reaches none (the job service) lists none. A provider that costs money is chosen only under max_cost, or when the job names it, and still runs only on the person's word for that route and its estimate.

dry_run.description: With true: what the host would do with the job or set, running nothing.

fabric.description: Where the statevector method's state runs: auto (the default: on a member only where the committed measurements show it faster than this host's CPU for the job's size and fusion width, otherwise on the CPU), cpu, accelerator (the first accelerator member certified bit-exact here that holds the state, falling back to the next if it fails during the run), a member's id or key (wai-quantum fabric lists them), or a list of members, a power of two of them, the state split by its top qubits into one partition on each (cpu is a member, and a member may be named more than once). A member certified bit-exact gives the CPU's bits. A placement this host cannot honour is refused (J013), never made elsewhere.

history.description: The program's history's account of the version the job runs: its digest, and the gates and lines in each hand. The receipt binds it; a history recomputes and checks it.

anyOf.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled, with its options.

items.description: One of distribution, equivalent, prepares or sampled, with its options.

intent.description: What the program must do, checked with the run: one intent or a list. The result's verdict says how far it was checked.

method.description: auto (the default: the strongest method the program admits), or a method by its name as the methods list names it; pulse runs a pulse program (OpenPulse calibrations) under the pulse options.

mitigate.description: Mitigate the job's expectation values (or, for readout, its counts) under its noise (engine::mitigate): zne, pea, pec, cdr, vd or readout, or {"method", …} with its options. The result's mitigation gives each value raw and mitigated.

noise.description: A noise model, each channel a probability. A channel not listed here is refused.

observables.description: Pauli observables to take the expectation values of.

anyOf.description: A Pauli string, as "Z0 Z1"; qubits count from 0.

options.description: Options of the method that runs the job, as the methods list names them (max_bond, cutoff, fusion, trajectories, threshold, max_weight, ladder, max_terms, path_restarts, controls), and memory_gb.

controls.description: A gate whose standard gates would double (x, y, z or h under three or more controls; s, sdg, t, tdg, p, rx, ry, rz, u, sx or sxdg under two or more) runs as one on statevector and in standard gates on exact. "standard" runs standard gates on statevector too, which reproduces a result made that way bit for bit. "whole" holds the gate whole on exact too, which gives other bits than its default, and is refused (J003) on a job that runs standard gates: another method named, a compile, noise, mitigation, a device target or a named place on the fabric. Any other value is refused.

params.description: A value for each of the program's parameters (`input float theta;`, `input angle phi;`), bound exactly before the program is read: it runs as if each were written as a `const` at that double. A parameter left without a value is refused (Q114, J050). In a sweep, the parameters it fixes, each bound at every point.

programs.description: A set (engine::sets): the programs to run as one job, each a program's text or a job of its own; the request's other fields apply to every item that does not set them itself.

anyOf.description: A program's text.
A job of its own, read as a job request is (no programs or sweep in it); each item of the set's result holds its request in full.

provider.description: The person's own provider to run on, by the name their registry gives it. Only a host that holds their credentials runs such a job; every other host refuses it.

pulse.description: A pulse run's options (method "pulse"): the sample period, the levels kept, the tolerance on the stated error, the steps a sample is divided into, each qubit's parameters, static couplings, and ports beyond the names d0, m0, a0.

levels.description: Levels kept per qubit (default 2; 3 shows leakage).

ports.description: Ports by name: what each is for and the qubit it reaches.

rabi_mhz.description: Its Rabi frequency at full amplitude, MHz.

qubits.description: Each qubit's parameters by its index, over the target's and the defaults.

substeps.description: Steps per sample (default: chosen so each step times the generator's norm is at most 0.5).

tolerance.description: The most the stated error may be (default 1e-6): a run whose bound and rounding estimate pass it is refused, naming the steps that would meet it.

qasm.description: The program, in OpenQASM 3 or the OpenQASM 2 forms in common use.

repair.description: Repair the program first on its flagged lines: true, or the choices.

seed.description: The sampling seed (1 when not given): the same job and seed give the same counts.

shots.description: Measurement shots; 1024 when no observables or amplitudes are asked for, otherwise 0.

source.description: The program in another format, in place of qasm (engine::formats::expand): read to the job's qasm before the job is read, the request keeping its source.

sweep.description: A set over the request's own qasm: values for each of the program's inputs (integer, float or angle), every combination run, the names in sorted order and the first varying slowest.

anyOf.description: A device target: its qubits, the pairs it couples, its native gates with their errors and durations, and the calibration snapshot they come from. A value not known is left out, never written as zero. Every field but format, name, source, qubits, gates and coupling is optional, and a field the format does not name is refused, so a misspelt one never reads as absent. Its canonical text is its RFC 8785 form, and the BLAKE3 of that text, the target's hash, names the snapshot in a receipt.

id.description: The calibration snapshot's id, as the source names it, or a content id of the snapshot read.

timestamp.description: When the snapshot was taken, as the source writes it.

coupling.description: The pairs a two-qubit gate may act on, each once, the lower qubit first, sorted.

gates.description: Each native gate where the device runs it, sorted by gate then qubits.

label.description: The source's own name for it, when that is not its index.

qubit.description: Its index: its place in the list.

t2_us.description: T2 (the echo or Ramsey time the source reports), microseconds.

format.description: The format the target was read from (wai-quantum targets import --help lists them).

turns_over_2_33.description: The phase exactly, in 2^33rds of a turn.

rounding_estimate.description: A pulse run: an estimate of floating-point rounding beside the bound, not a proof.

t_count.description: stabilizer_rank: the T and T† gates the program lowers to.

bound.description: A bound on |exact − value| of the amplitude, holding with the probability confidence states (stabilizer_rank's sampled mode).

calibration.description: A provider job: the calibration snapshot it ran under.

anyOf.description: A provider job: the program sent, compiled exactly to the device's own gates: its basis (the device's gate set), its OpenQASM 3 text (qasm3) and that text's BLAKE3 (program), its counts of gates and swaps, its layouts, and the check it passed before it was sent. Results sealed before qasm3 carry the hash alone.

placement.description: Where the program was placed on the device's qubits, and why.

qasm3.description: The program sent, as OpenQASM 3, $i being index i of the coupling map the provider described; program is the BLAKE3 of its UTF-8 bytes.

qubit_names.description: The device's own name for each index the program uses, as it was when the job was sent, where a client sends it under those names.

anyOf.description: A job asked to compile its program first: what ran is the compiled circuit, within distance of the program in the operator norm up to a global phase.

basis.description: The gate set the program was compiled to.

certificate.description: The BLAKE3 of the compile certificate's RFC 8785 text, in hex.

distance.description: The bound the passes' distances add to.

output.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

source.description: A circuit's counts, as the compiler counts them.

compiled.description: How the program was compiled before it ran: on the person's own provider, to the device's gates; or, asked with compile, to a basis within a budget. Either way, basis is the gate set it was compiled to.

components.description: The identity of every component that made the result, when a registered one took part (engine::registry): its program's format, the passes its compile ran, the noise channels it names, its method; each registered one marked so. Sealed by the receipt with the rest.

items.description: One component that made the result (engine::registry): its kind, name and version, the BLAKE3 digest of its descriptor, and whether it is built in. A result carries these only when a registered component took part; one made by built-ins alone names them as it always has (its method, its compile's passes, its noise's channels and the engine's version), the digests of that version listed by the components list.

certified.description: Beside a registered component: the engine does not certify it.

digest.description: BLAKE3 of the component's descriptor in its canonical JSON (engine::registry::digest_of).

origin.description: built-in: the engine's own; registered: a host's own, added in its process, not part of the engine.

cost.description: A provider job: the estimate shown before it was sent, what the provider says it charged, and whether the person confirmed a run that was not free.

counts.description: Outcomes and their counts, keyed by the program's classical bits, the highest bit first. At most 65536 outcomes are listed; omitted_shots holds the rest.

counts_source.description: A provider job: where its counts come from (wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.3): tallied from one record a shot (shots), the provider's own counts (vendor_counts), or rebuilt from the probabilities it returned by largest remainders, derived and not shot records (probabilities). Results sealed before it carry neither it nor execution.

diagnostics.description: The reader's warnings and notes on the program, each with its code.

class.description: bit-exact: the same bits on every machine; exact: no approximation beyond double-precision rounding; single: single-precision arithmetic; bounded: a rigorous bound beside each value; estimate: a statistical estimate with its standard error; heuristic: an approximation with an estimate of its error, not a bound; measured: counts a processor returned through the person's provider, not reproducible by recomputation; simulated: counts a provider's simulator or emulator returned, measured on no device. radians.description: The same in radians, in (-pi, pi].

anyOf.description: A job: queued, running, done with its result and receipt, or failed with its error; a set's job holds the set's result; with dry_run true, what the service would do with it, running nothing.

A write's job (POST /v1/write, write_circuit): queued; running, with the attempts checked so far; done, its result the transcript, sealed, with its timing beside it; or failed, cancelled or interrupted, saying why.

digests.description: The BLAKE3 digests the store keeps the write's objects under: its request, its result and its receipt.

memory_bytes.description: What it holds of the jobs' memory budget: none, since the writer's memory is its own, held to its own cap.

work.description: The most tokens its replies may take.

interruptions.description: Each time the service stopped while the write ran, in milliseconds since 1970; it is run again, once, from its stored request, and gives the same transcript.

peak_rss_bytes.description: The most memory the writer process held while it wrote, its model's mapped pages among it.

progress.description: While it runs: how many attempts the engine has checked, and the latest.

latest.description: One attempt of a write: the program the model's reply gave, its digest, and the engine's check of it against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model.

answered.description: Whether the reply gave a program: false for one that ended inside its thinking, of which the engine had nothing to check.

check.description: The engine's check of the program against the task (wai.quantum.course-check/1, its lesson null), whose what_went_wrong went back to the model; null when the reply gave no program.

level.description: The level the engine checked the program to; null where there is none.

thinking_closed.description: Whether the reply reached the thinking cap still thinking, and had its thinking closed for it.

thinking_tokens.description: The reply's tokens that were thinking, counted on the tokens it gave: up to and including the one that ended its thinking, all of a reply whose thinking did not end.

request.description: What a write asks: its task, and how many repairs and tokens a reply may take; kept as its canonical text (RFC 8785), which its receipt binds.

max_new.description: The most tokens one reply may take, its thinking included (default 3000).

task.description: The task: an exercise in the course's form (wai.quantum.exercise/1), with an intent, or cases that each have one.

result.description: A write's result: its transcript (wai.quantum.write/1), with the energy the writer spent on it and the service's receipt, which seals the rest with the write's request. The transcript names the task and its digest, the model by its name, licence and the digest of its files with how far they were checked and the arithmetic it ran in, the prompt by its version and digests, the decoding with its thinking cap, the memory each check's run was planned in, the engine, and each attempt with the engine's check; the same model, task, options and engine give the same transcript in the same arithmetic, so anyone who holds the model can write it again on a host whose architecture, operating system, maths library and matmul kernel are the model's here, and compare.

think_max.description: The most tokens of a reply that may be thinking: a reply still thinking there has its thinking closed for it and answers in the tokens left.

service_kwh.description: A provider job: the provider's own figure.

attribution.description: Whose energy it is: the job's worker process, or none (the processor packages' over the job's window, every process on the host in it).

concurrent_jobs.description: Other jobs that ran on the host during the window.

counter.description: The package counter as seen: the longest it went between updates, and the smallest step it took.

declared.description: What the stated uncertainty covers, and what it does not.

energy.description: The CPU energy of the job's process as the kernel counts it, with its uncertainty and what it leaves out, or unmetered with the reason.

engine.description: The version of the engine (wai-quantum) that checked each attempt.

arch.description: The architecture the model ran on (Rust's target_arch).

checked.description: How far the model's files were checked against its manifest before they were loaded: their sizes, or every byte (BLAKE3). The model loads exactly the files the manifest lists either way. A scripted model has none.

matmul.description: The BF16 matmul kernel its projections took there, which fixes the arithmetic of every logit; greedy decoding gives the same tokens again only in the same.

os.description: The operating system it ran on, whose maths library its exponentials come from.

passed_round.description: The round whose program passed; null when none did.
